zugrpc

Overview

gRPC is how many services talk to each other, Spark Connect among them. It runs only over HTTP/2 and puts each call’s status in HTTP trailers, which the usual R HTTP clients do not expose. Until now, calling a gRPC service from R meant installing the gRPC C++ libraries or going through Python.

zugrpc is a gRPC client written in R. It speaks the gRPC wire protocol over the HTTP/2 requests that zuhttp makes, so it needs no gRPC, protobuf or libcurl installed on the system. You encode and decode messages yourself, typically with zuproto.

  • Unary and server-streaming calls. grpc_call() returns one message; grpc_stream() returns them one at a time as they arrive, and the server sends only as fast as you read.
  • Errors you can select by class. Every status code is a condition class, such as zugrpc_error_unavailable, and the google.rpc.Status details, Spark’s ErrorInfo among them, are decoded for you.
  • Deadlines and cancellation. A deadline goes to the server as grpc-timeout and also bounds the call locally. Cancelling a stream resets it with RST_STREAM and keeps the connection for other calls.
  • zuhttp’s transport. Cleartext HTTP/2 for local servers, TLS with the platform’s own TLS stack and trust store, a connection pool and HTTP/2 keepalive.

Installation

zugrpc is not on CRAN yet. Install the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zugrpc")

Usage 

library(zugrpc)

These examples talk to a fake server, built from zuhttp’s mock transport, with plain-text messages instead of protobuf. Against a real server, leave out client = fake.

A channel holds what every call to one server shares.

ch <- grpc_channel("http://localhost:50051", client = fake)

A unary call sends one request message and returns one response.

res <- grpc_call(ch, "/demo.Greeter/SayHello", charToRaw("world"), deadline = 5)
rawToChar(res$message)
#> [1] "hello, world"

A server-streaming call yields its messages one at a time, then NULL.

st <- grpc_stream(ch, "/demo.Greeter/Count", raw())
while (!is.null(m <- st$next_message())) print(rawToChar(m))
#> [1] "one"
#> [1] "two"
#> [1] "three"
st$status()
#> [1] "OK"

A failed call raises a condition whose class names its status.

tryCatch(
  grpc_call(ch, "/demo.Greeter/SayGoodbye", raw()),
  zugrpc_error_not_found = function(cnd) cnd$grpc_message
)
#> [1] "no such greeting"

Every function starts with grpc_, except zugrpc_info(), and a failed call’s condition class is zugrpc_error_ followed by its status code in lower case.

Related work

zugrpc follows gRPC’s HTTP/2 protocol and status codes. It is tested against grpc-go’s interop server and against Spark Connect. It bundles the google/rpc protocol definitions from googleapis to decode error details. rgrpc is a client and server built on the gRPC C++ libraries.
